solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Annoying to see the rooms let out and be on the fringes

indicators.note: the two letters of 'be' sit at the edges, around the rest
rooms that are let out are rearranged among tenants, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A landlord finds viewing the rentable rooms and hanging about on the periphery a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' reads as renting rooms but signals the anagram; 'on the fringes' places the two letters of 'be' at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irksome that causes trouble is a synonym-level match for annoying.

clue.text: 'Contest' with second letter missing

parts.note: B is the second letter of the alphabet
someone missing is out, not present

explanation.surface: An editor notes that the word 'contest' has lost its second letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks make 'Contest' look like a word to be edited; it is simply the definition, and 'second letter' means the alphabet's, not the word's.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing or wrestling match is a contest, a common sporting synonym.

clue.text: Will try to get at people trapped within

parts.note: to try something is to test it

indicators.note: the people are caught inside the two letters of 'at'

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to reach people stuck inside somewhere, out of sheer determination.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal document leaving one's estate is a last will, a synonym.

clue.text: Run a newspaper

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide or bye
a special edition of a newspaper, as in the old street cry of the paper seller

explanation.surface: Someone takes on the management of a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bye or wide is a bonus run, and a special late edition of a paper bears the same name.

clue.text: Supports losers?

definitions.meaning: to support a motion is to second it, so supports are this verb's third-person form
those finishing in second place are runners-up, not winners

explanation.surface: A cynic asks whether people who back someone are simply backing the losing side.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a proposal is to second it; those who come second rather than first have lost.

clue.text: Small point in transcript

parts.note: minute means tiny
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A tiny detail turns up in a written record.
explanation.definitionFit: The written record of a meeting is called its minutes, a written account of what was said.

clue.text: Silent call — a number's engaged

indicators.note: the number is held inside the call, like a fiance taken up by it

parts.note: to dub is to call or name someone
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A phone call goes unanswered because the line is busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' reads as a busy phone line but signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable or unwilling to speak; mute is the sense shared with silent.

clue.text: What we normally do when having time by ourselves

indicators.note: by means next to, so the time stands beside ourselves

parts.note: us is the plain pronoun for ourselves
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A description of people's habits when they have time alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Customary practice, habitual behaviour, is what usage describes.

clue.text: Cured one's inside, though no doctor?

indicators.note: the word for one's goes inside the word for cured

parts.note: someone cured is better
one's read as ONES

explanation.surface: A patient's innards have been healed, though not by any doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional manipulator of fractures and joints who lacks a medical qualification, hence not a doctor.

clue.text: Leading by some games: unexpected result

parts.note: a player leading is up
in tennis a set is a group of games

explanation.surface: A tennis commentator notes a lead by a few games and a surprising outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock victory over the favourite is called an upset in sport.

clue.text: Anti air force

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a strain is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A protester opposes the air force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air force' looks like one unit; the split is 'air' then the verb 'force'.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel or restrict someone is to constrain them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Not serious nuisance to contain ivy that needs docking

indicators.note: the nuisance holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a trial is a trouble or nuisance

indicators.note: docking cuts off the tail, so the last letter of ivy goes

explanation.surface: A gardener's trivial pest is ivy that needs cutting back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trifling and unimportant is lightweight, the synonym for not serious.

clue.text: On the other side silver satin, shimmering

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: shimmering suggests the letters dancing and shifting about

explanation.surface: Shimmering silver satin is set off on the opposite side.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposed, contrary or in opposition means on the other side of an argument.

clue.text: One day by sea changed views

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: changed means the letters of sea are altered in order

explanation.surface: A single day at the seaside changed someone's opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: Notions and opinions are synonyms, as in sharing one's thoughts on a subject.

clue.text: He's had to have one because I wasn't there

definitions.text: He's had to have one because I wasn't there

parts.words: He's had to have one because I wasn't there
parts.note: the contraction of he is drops the letter I, and a punctuation mark stands where it was

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a man was forced to do something because the speaker was absent.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark marks a dropped letter, here the I missing from he is.

clue.text: Final note about contract to hire suits

indicators.note: the postscript goes round the contract

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter
a lease is a contract to rent property

explanation.surface: A last memo on a rental agreement for hiring out suits of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suits' looks like clothing to hire but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: If something suits you it gratifies or satisfies you, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Retailers will need large quantities of wine, getting quotation

indicators.note: quoting is repeating words as spoken, so the stores of wine are given as they sound

parts.note: a cellar is a stock of wine

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers need big stocks of wine and are getting a price quote.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers who sell goods are vendors, the plain meaning of retailers.

clue.text: A bit tipsy, I spent penny coming in

indicators.note: the penny enters the jumbled letters
a tipsy person staggers, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A slightly drunk person confesses to having spent a penny, British slang for using the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit tipsy' looks like one phrase; 'A bit' is the definition, 'tipsy' the anagram signal on ISPENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fragment or scrap of something is a bit, a synonym.

clue.text: Hard getting through at first. Don't give up

indicators.note: the word for through is placed at the front

parts.note: per means through or by means of
severe means hard or harsh

explanation.surface: Encouragement: it is tough to get through at the start, but keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist and keep going is to refuse to quit, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Is one fixing on staying?

parts.note: to settle is both to fix or decide and to make a home somewhere, so one who does it is fixing on staying

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone has decided to remain.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist who makes a permanent home somewhere has decided on remaining there.

clue.text: Gets wound up again and backs off

definitions.meaning: to flinch or shrink away in horror

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry again and then retreats.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re plus coils it means is wound once more; as one word it means draws back in alarm.

clue.text: Tortured, I reveal woman's name

indicators.note: tortured letters are twisted out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Under torture, someone gives up a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female given name, an example of a woman's name.

clue.text: Mistakenly given another case of wine that's gone off

indicators.note: mistakenly suggests the letters are set out wrongly
the case of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: A customer is wrongly sent a second case of wine that has turned sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour wine turns acetic, and the name of the condiment literally means sour wine.

clue.text: High point of game from which Black withdrew

indicators.note: the letter for black is pulled out of the game

parts.note: bridge is a card game
B is the abbreviation for black, as in pencil grades

explanation.surface: A tense moment in a chess game as Black retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: Black looks like a chess player; it is only the letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: A long raised crest of land, such as a hill ridge, is a high point.

clue.text: Lay about feeling unhappy?

parts.note: a lay is a song, and a mournful song of lament is about grief

explanation.surface: Reads like a description of someone lounging around feeling glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay about' suggests a layabout, an idler; here a lay is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral lament is a song expressing sorrow, a lay about unhappiness.

clue.text: Use up ice cream, problem for storage

indicators.note: the problem is stored inside the ice cream

parts.note: an ice cream cone, often just called a cone
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Finish the ice cream, because keeping it is a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat or exhaust something entirely is to use it up, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Mixed bar in a French town

definitions.note: town used adjectivally, as in town life, matching an adjective

indicators.note: the mixed letters go inside the French word

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of bar are stirred together

explanation.surface: A French town has a bar with a mixed crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a city or built-up area is the adjectival sense of town, as in town planning.

clue.text: Discharge when spell in jail's up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

explanation.surface: A prisoner is released when the sentence has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads as finished, but in a down clue it turns the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To give off or send out, as a chimney gives off smoke, is to discharge.

clue.text: Blasted freezing!

definitions.meaning: a mild British curse word, like damned or bloody

explanation.surface: An exclamation about bitterly cold weather.
explanation.definitionFit: British speech uses the word both as a mild expletive and to mean bitterly cold.

clue.text: Ray hooks river creature

indicators.note: the ray catches the river letter inside it

parts.note: a beam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: A fisherman named Ray lands a river creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a fish or an angler's name; it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish is an example of a creature.

clue.text: Heavens! Has lost with flush!

indicators.note: the word Heavens loses the letters of has, scattered through it

explanation.surface: A card player exclaims in dismay at losing to a flush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flush' suggests poker, but it means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Flush with the wall means level with it, a synonym.

clue.text: Neat knots to keep cord from tightening

indicators.note: the knotted letters hold the cord within them
knotting twists the letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: string is a cord

explanation.surface: Tidy knots stop a cord from being pulled tight.
explanation.definitionFit: An astringent substance contracts body tissue, a tightening effect.
